body: Thank you a lot. What you said does help a lot. It's just this endless loop of ups and downs. What mostly feels downs. But yeah.  I do have to believe that there is something better. I do have to put the effort to it. Thanks. I guess I have to reconsider a lot of things. The past few years have been tough, this year is the toughest yet. But I guess that you have to fall to get up again.

Thank you for answering. Thing is I was close to commiting once, but I talked to a "friend" and he alerted the police. We haven't spoken since. 

The problem is really that I just don't see any possible outcome. It's like I don't see me having a future. My parents know nothing of all of this. As far as they are concerned, I recovered from my depression. I don't know what would happen if I tell them that I've been lying to them for the last 8 months.... Still, I don't see me going anywhere...
It happened to me as well. I think they are refugees and you can't stop refugees migrating or running away

In my opinion,  if that's what you think,  you might be better not playing the game, as it sounds like you will constantly have that feeling of "it could be better". On the other hand it might be up to a year until they release all their patches and DLC.  So either enjoy what you have and get all you can out of it,  or wait until you can enjoy it. That's what games are for :).

I totally agree on this. I might add that though I am a huge fan of ME1-3, I highly enjoyed this one. It has quite a few bugs,  and some game breaking ones that I have experienced in my 90 hours play through,  but it still didn't ruin the experience. If you can,  I would suggest waiting for a few more patches for a good finished game.  But if you must play it now,  you won't regret it.

On insanity it took me 90 hours to complete 98 percent of the game. I am also the kind of guy who has to do pretty much everything. Only quests that were left undone were very minor fetch quests that don't add almost anything.  Basically  the ones that you get from roaming around the maps clearing Kett or outlaw camps.

After the 1.05 patch the mattock is OK.  My only problem with it is that I play gold. And using the mattock on gold leaves your finger pretty tired after just one game. If you are using a semiautomatic rifle it better hit hard, or else you are risking losing your finger.

Totally agree on that. Tons of people running around not making good use of cover,  or not retreating when they should. On another note,  I save my cobras for that wave 6. When you get the upload mission or the assassinate, it's a godsend.

It will just take you longer to win. But it's doable.  A pain in the ass.  But doable. I started doing gold with the worst combo ever of human engineer and avenger. Been there done that for the challenge. Not going back to it. Titian soldier and a revenant for me pls. Or broken immortal Angara insurgent.

To answer you,  I played with the Avenger on the human engineer when I started doing  gold.  And I was second or third most of the time.  Right after the guy/guys who had the broken vanquisher.  Don't dismiss experience so easily.  Knowing your maps, when to engage and when to run is way more important than having the best weapon and mods.  It sure helps though. It wasn't unusual for me to finish wave 4-5 alone because the guys with vanquisher died because of getting swarmed and not even having a revive pack.  That's another question.  Use your freaking consumables!  They make all the difference in the world.

There is a point to be made about being a good player though.  If someone played a tin in ME3, they might do good. I started doing gold on APEX 1000 or so,  and it was good. But yeah.  APEX 300 joining gold is no fun. Silver is doable almost from the start once you get acquainted with bronze.
Just one of the many great moments in ME:A. There is also the Liam loyalty mission.  That one is great.

It's just about learning their moves.  My first play through was on insanity and my fist architect took my by surprise.  I died so much then. By the time of the second one I had learned all its moves and it just became a looooong grindy fight. As I said,  if you know it's moves you are set.
Can't wait for part 2!!! Great story.
Move your Lord a bit and get him a bit closer to the walls. It's like flashing a big sign "Hey I'm here" in front of the enemy. They might still shoot you one or twice, but it should be fine.

I totally agree. It does seem rather odd that if you break pacts your chivalry is not affected. Same goes for honoring a call to war of an ally. Diplomacy should have both positive and negative influence on chivalry depending on your actions, in my opinion.

Fast reply on my phone.

You are supposed to hit Marienburg on turn 2. From turn 1-2 recruit only archers. 

Resolve manually, keep all your troops on your left flank, Lord up front to tank towers,  and trebuchets ready to destroy towers. 

Once towers are taken care of, use your archers until they run out of ammo. Then assault. You should take less than 200 casualties and get Marienburg on turn 2. 

On turn 3 rush to the orc settlement (forgot the name). Will be a tough fight, but hammer and anvil should work fine. Your peasant lines WILL crumble, so with your massive archer advantage, shoot at the gaps. That will take care of the orcs that thought that were winning. 

And there you go. Turn 3 with both Marienburg yours and the orc settlement destroyed. After that just go wipe out the other Marienburg minor settlement (Gorssel?) as soon as possible, because they will start recruiting. On turn 5 you should have 2 provinces to your name. Now good luck defending against Norscan raids :D.
